# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to
Semantic Versioning.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.11.0] - 2026-08-18

### Added

- Add v2 organization create and update options for website, LinkedIn URL,
  industry, annual revenue and employee count, including explicit clear options
  for nullable values.
- Add v2 person create and update options for postal address, notes, instant
  messaging accounts, birthday and job title. `PersonAddress` is an alias of
  `OrganizationAddress`, preserving compatibility with existing address values.
- Add v1 support for the `nova` and `partnership` permission-set app values and
  the `nova` user-access app value.

### Changed

- Refresh the official v1 and v2 OpenAPI specifications, re-derive the v1
  legacy surface and regenerate the internal clients.

## [1.10.1] - 2026-08-14

### Changed

- Bump the preferred Go toolchain, CI, security scanning and OpenAPI drift
  checks from Go 1.26.5 to Go 1.26.6. Go 1.25 remains supported.
- Bump `github/codeql-action` from v4.37.5 to v4.37.6, keeping the `init`
  and `analyze` steps on the same pinned revision.

## [1.10.0] - 2026-08-07

### Security

- Credentials from `Config.Auth` are now attached only to requests whose origin
  matches `Config.BaseURL`. Previously the transport middleware re-applied them
  on every redirect hop, so a cross-origin redirect delivered `x-api-token` and
  OAuth bearer tokens to the redirect target. An unparseable `BaseURL` now fails
  closed and no credentials are sent at all. With an empty `Config.BaseURL`
  credentials still apply to every first-party request, but a redirect leaving
  the initial request's origin suppresses them on that hop.
- Credential headers set directly on a request (for example through
  `WithHeader("x-api-token", …)`) are stripped when a redirect leaves the pinned
  origin. `NewHTTPClient` installs a `CheckRedirect` for this; a `CheckRedirect`
  already present on a supplied `HTTPClient` is still called, and the standard
  10-redirect limit is preserved. Credential headers the preserved callback
  re-adds to an off-origin hop are removed again after it returns.
- The v1 OAuth client is built without the `Auth` provider, so an API token is
  no longer sent to the OAuth host.
- Non-2xx response bodies are truncated at 1 MiB. They previously bypassed the
  response size cap entirely and were buffered in full into `APIError.Body`.
- A server-supplied `Retry-After` is capped and no longer overflows when
  converted to a duration.

  Project Templates and Project Fields.

  Deals, Persons, Organizations, Products, Activities and Fields.

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- v1 `Files.Add` now takes the file name and a content reader
  (`Add(ctx, fileName, content, opts...)`) and builds the multipart body
  itself, mirroring `CallLogs.AddRecording`; callers no longer encode
  multipart by hand. This is a breaking signature change. New
  `WithFileDealID`, `WithFilePersonID`, `WithFileOrganizationID`,
  `WithFileProductID`, `WithFileActivityID` and `WithFileLeadID` options
  associate the uploaded file with an item.

### Fixed

- v1 `Files.Add` uploads now retry on 429 (and on 502/503/504 with
  `RetryPolicy.RetryAllMethods`). The multipart body is encoded in memory,
  so the request has a replayable `GetBody`; previously a caller-supplied
  streaming body such as an `*os.File` could not be replayed, so the retry
  transport declined to retry and the upload failed on the first
  rate-limit response.

part.text:
Done. Branch `fix/files-add-retry` with 3 focused commits; working tree clean, full suite green.

## Root cause

`Files.Add` accepted a caller-built `io.Reader` and passed it straight through to `http.NewRequest`. For an `*os.File` (or a hand-streamed multipart body), `req.GetBody` is nil, so the retry transport — by design — refuses to replay the request and the 429 surfaced immediately. Every other call retries fine because their bodies are `bytes.Reader`/`strings.Reader`, which get a working `GetBody`.

## PR notes

**Summary**
- `Files.Add` now mirrors `CallLogs.AddRecording`: `Add(ctx, fileName, content, opts...)` — the SDK builds the multipart body itself (field name `file`, per the v1 spec).
- The body is encoded in memory via `internal/multipartbody`, producing a `*bytes.Reader` with a working `GetBody`, so uploads now retry on 429 (any method) and on 502/503/504 with `RetryPolicy{RetryAllMethods: true}`.
- Extended `internal/multipartbody` with `NewFileWithFields` / `Field` for plain form parts alongside the file part; `NewFile` is unchanged in behavior.
- New association options replacing what callers previously hand-encoded: `WithFileDealID`, `WithFilePersonID`, `WithFileOrganizationID`, `WithFileProductID`, `WithFileActivityID`, `WithFileLeadID`.
- Changelog updated under `[Unreleased]`.

**Testing performed**
- TDD: wrote failing tests first, then implemented.
- New regression test reproduces the exact report: upload body from `os.Open`, `RetryAllMethods: true`, server answers 429 then 200 — asserts 2 attempts with byte-identical replayed bodies.
- Coverage for multipart structure (field/file name, payload), association form fields, validation (empty name / nil content, no request sent), and source-read errors; `multipartbody` unit tests including the `GetBody` replay property.
- `go test ./...`, `go test -race` on affected packages, `gofmt -l`, `go vet` — all clean (golangci-lint unavailable offline: `GOPROXY=off`).

**Breaking changes / migration**
- `Files.Add` signature changed from `Add(ctx, body io.Reader, contentType string, opts...)` to `Add(ctx, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts...)`. Migration: drop the hand-built multipart body and content type, pass the file name and reader, and move any association IDs into the new `WithFile*ID` options. `Raw().Do` remains as an escape hatch for exotic encodings.
